x.t: Helpers move people to safety before storm Akvan
b: More than 70,000 people in Odisha have been moved to safety early. They can stay in [[shelter|shelters]], which are safe places.
Akvan is a [[cyclone|cyclone]], a large storm over the sea. The [[forecast|forecast]] says it is likely to cross the coast by Friday 20 November.
In Odisha, rescue teams have been sent out to help. Schools in six districts are closed from Thursday to Saturday because of the storm.

o.t: Odisha moves more than 70,000 people to safety ahead of Akvan
b: By Thursday 19 November, more than 70,000 people in Odisha had been moved to safety ahead of [[cyclone|Cyclone]] Akvan, a large storm over the Bay of Bengal. [[shelter|Shelters]], safe places where people can stay, are open for them.

A [[forecast|forecast]] is a statement of what is expected to happen. Thursday's forecast said Akvan is likely to cross the coast between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha by around noon on Friday 20 November. Winds of 90 to 100 kilometres an hour are expected as it crosses.

In Odisha, rescue teams have been deployed, which means organised and sent out to do a particular job. Schools in six districts are closed from Thursday 19 to Saturday 21 November. Three trains were rescheduled, which means their times were changed, because of the approaching storm.

stories.think: Many helpers are at work this week, from weather forecasters to rescue teams. Which helper's job would you like to know more about, and why?

x.t: Countries start a big check on climate progress
b: Countries are at [[cop|COP31]], a big climate meeting in Türkiye. On Wednesday, a check on progress began there.
It is called the [[global-stocktake|Global Stocktake]]. It checks how countries are doing together on climate. A check shows what still needs work.
Countries are also writing a climate deal. A new [[draft|draft]], an early version, was due on Thursday. The meeting is set to end on Friday.

o.t: COP31: Global Stocktake begins as talks near their scheduled end
b: The second [[global-stocktake|Global Stocktake]] was launched on Wednesday 18 November at [[cop|COP31]], the climate talks in Antalya, Türkiye. It checks the progress countries are making together on climate change.

That day, [[minister|ministers]], senior members of governments, held a closed meeting called a Divan. Countries are also writing a climate deal. A new [[draft|draft]], or early version, was due on Thursday 19 November. Countries are divided over what it should say about [[fossil-fuels|fossil fuels]] (coal, oil and gas). Some fossil fuel-producing countries oppose wording on moving away from them.

Some countries have set out national plans to exit fossil fuels, including France, Germany, Finland, Denmark and the Netherlands. About 75 countries are said to back a promise to raise electricity's share of energy use to 35% by 2035. The talks are scheduled to close on Friday 20 November.

stories.think: The Global Stocktake checks how the world is doing so far. When you are working on something big, how does stopping to check your progress help?

a: A vote on who hosts the next meeting
A check on how countries are doing on climate
The final version of the climate deal

x.t: Eight old teeth tell a story about early humans
b: Scientists found eight [[fossil|fossil]] teeth in two caves in southern China. A fossil is the remains of a living thing from long ago.
The teeth suggest that [[homo-erectus|Homo erectus]], an early kind of human, lived there. That was between 324,000 and 184,000 years ago.
The teeth hold other clues. They show these early humans lived in [[rainforest|rainforest]]. Scientists had not recorded them in rainforest before.

o.t: Fossil teeth suggest early humans lived in a rainforest in China
b: Eight [[fossil|fossil]] teeth from two caves in [[guangxi|Guangxi]], in southern China, suggest that [[homo-erectus|Homo erectus]], an early kind of human, lived there between 324,000 and 184,000 years ago. A fossil is the remains or trace of an animal or plant that lived long ago. The research was published in the journal Nature on Wednesday 18 November.
The caves, named Baxian and Naxian, are about 15 kilometres apart. Before this, Homo erectus was thought to have vanished from mainland Asia around 400,000 years ago.

The chemistry of the teeth shows that these early humans lived in [[rainforest|rainforest]]. That is a habitat, or natural home, not previously recorded for this species, or kind of living thing. Chemical clues in the teeth also suggest that some individuals moved over large areas, possibly towards northern Vietnam.

stories.think: These teeth gave scientists new clues about the past. Can you think of a time when a new clue changed what you thought about something?

quiz.q: How many fossil teeth from the two caves do scientists link to Homo erectus?

x.t: Two New Zealand batters fight back against India
b: India's cricket team is playing New Zealand in a [[test-match|Test match]]. It began on Thursday at the [[basin-reserve|Basin Reserve]] in Wellington.
India's bowlers started well. They got five batters out when New Zealand had 70 runs.
Then Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips batted together for the rest of the day. Nicholls made 113 runs. One batter scoring 100 or more is a [[century|century]]. New Zealand ended day one on 243.

o.t: Nicholls century lifts New Zealand to 243 for 5 against India
b: New Zealand were 243 for 5 at the end of day one of the first [[test-match|Test match]] against India, at the [[basin-reserve|Basin Reserve]] in Wellington, on Thursday 19 November. A Test is a cricket match between the teams of two different countries, with play spread over up to five days.
India bowled first and took five early [[wicket|wickets]], which means they got five batters out. That left New Zealand on 70 for 5. India's Jasprit Bumrah took three wickets for 52 runs.

Then Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips batted together for the rest of the day. Nicholls made a [[century|century]], 100 runs or more, and ended the day on 113 not out, meaning he has not been got out. Phillips was 94 not out. Their partnership, the runs two batters add together, is worth 173 so far. The match is not finished, so both can bat on.

stories.think: New Zealand lost five batters early, but two players kept going for the rest of the day. What helps you keep going when something starts badly?

quiz.q: How many runs had Henry Nicholls made by the end of day one?

x.t: Scientists study whales using only their breath
b: Scientists flew a small [[drone|drone]] through the breath of humpback whales off Canada. The drone carried clean dishes to catch the breath.
The breath held the whales' [[dna|DNA]]. DNA carries the information for how a living thing is made up. The scientists read whole sets of it.
No darts were needed, and boats did not have to come close. Next, the team plans to study the whales' family ties.

o.t: Scientists read whale DNA from breath caught by a drone
b: Scientists have sequenced the whole [[genome|genomes]] of humpback whales from the animals' breath. A genome is the complete set of [[dna|DNA]] in a living thing, and to sequence it is to work out the order of its chemical parts. DNA is the molecule in cells that carries the information for how a living thing is made up. The study was published in the journal Molecular Ecology Resources on Tuesday 17 November.

The team, which included scientists from the University of St Andrews, attached sterile, or germ-free, dishes to a small [[drone|drone]]. They flew it through the whales' exhaled breath off [[british-columbia|British Columbia]], Canada, and collected 58 samples from 26 whales. The work needed no darts and no close boat approaches.
The drone data correctly showed whether each whale was male or female. The team plans to use the genomes to study the whales' family ties and social bonds.

stories.think: If you could study a wild animal without going near it, which animal would you choose, and what would you want to find out?

quiz.q: What carried the dishes through the whales' breath?

x.t: Three leaders meet in China to talk
b: The leaders of three countries met in China on Thursday. The countries are the United States, China and Russia.
They met in a city called [[shenzhen|Shenzhen]]. News reports call it the first meeting of its kind.
When leaders meet, they can talk about problems face to face. Talking is not the same as agreeing.

o.t: Leaders of the US, China and Russia hold a three-way meeting
b: US President Donald Trump, China's President Xi Jinping and Russia's President Vladimir Putin met together in [[shenzhen|Shenzhen]], China, on Thursday 19 November. News reports describe it as the first three-way meeting of the leaders of the United States, China and Russia.

A meeting of three sides is called [[trilateral|trilateral]], and a meeting of two sides is [[bilateral|bilateral]]. Earlier on Thursday, Mr Trump held separate bilateral meetings with Mr Xi and with Mr Putin. The meetings took place at the [[apec|APEC]] [[summit|summit]], a meeting of leaders. APEC is short for Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation. It has 21 members, known as economies.

The talks were not expected to produce major agreements, news reports said. A meeting gives leaders a chance to talk face to face. It is not the same as an agreement, which is an arrangement about what to do that all sides accept.

stories.think: When you disagree with someone, what helps you sit down and talk it through with them?

quiz.q: What is a meeting of three sides called?

x.t: A giant star may have swallowed a smaller star
b: Astronomers are scientists who study space. They have been watching a giant star in the Andromeda [[galaxy|galaxy]].
The star is about 2.5 million [[light-year|light-years]] away. A light-year is how far light travels in one year.
The team first noticed the unusual star in 2023. Late in 2025, it gave off a burst of light. Astronomers say the giant star swallowed its smaller partner star.

o.t: Astronomers say a giant star in Andromeda swallowed its partner
b: Astronomers say they have caught a giant star swallowing its smaller companion, the other star in its pair. The two stars are in the Andromeda [[galaxy|galaxy]], about 2.5 million [[light-year|light-years]] away. A galaxy is a very large group of stars, and a light-year is the distance light travels in one year. The study was published in the journal Nature on Wednesday 18 November.

The giant star was about seven times the Sun's [[mass|mass]], the amount of matter in it. The team first noticed the star as unusual in 2023. Older records show it began growing more luminous, or brighter, in 2018.

Late in 2025, the star erupted in a burst of light. The [[james-webb|James Webb Space Telescope]] observed it in December 2025. Another telescope, the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, could find more events like this.

stories.think: Astronomers first noticed this star in 2023 and kept watching it. What would you be willing to watch patiently for a long time, and why?

quiz.q: About how far away is the giant star?

b: [[pv-sindhu|PV Sindhu]] plays badminton. New [[world-ranking|world rankings]] came out on Tuesday. The rankings are a list that puts players in order by results.
Sindhu is now fifth in women's singles. Singles means one player against one. She was last in the top five in November 2022.

o.t: PV Sindhu returns to badminton's world top five after four years
b: Indian badminton player [[pv-sindhu|PV Sindhu]] is back in the world's top five. In the women's singles [[world-ranking|world rankings]] released on Tuesday 17 November, she is placed fifth, after moving up one place. Singles means one player against one player. It is her first time in the top five since November 2022.

The world rankings are a list that puts players in order by their results. Sindhu has risen six places in the last 45 days, from 11th to fifth. Her recent results include winning the HYLO Open and finishing as [[runner-up|runner-up]], which means second, at the French Open. She also won the Japan Open in 2026.
Sindhu has qualified for the [[bwf-world-tour-finals|BWF World Tour Finals]], which means she has earned a place. It is the 2026 season finale, the last event of the badminton season.

stories.think: PV Sindhu waited four years to get back into the top five. What is something you would keep working at, even if it took a long time?

quiz.q: Where is PV Sindhu placed in the new women's singles world rankings?

b: A big group of robots danced together on Tuesday 17 November. There were 151 of them. They danced in [[shenzhen|Shenzhen]], a city in China.
They were [[humanoid|humanoid]] robots. Humanoid means shaped like a human.
The dance set a [[guinness-world-record|Guinness World Record]]. A world record is the best anyone has done at something. This one is about how many humanoid robots dance together.

o.t: 151 dancing robots in Shenzhen set a Guinness World Record
b: On Tuesday 17 November, 151 [[humanoid|humanoid]] robots danced together in [[shenzhen|Shenzhen]], a city in China. Humanoid means shaped like a human, so each of these machines was built in the form of a human body.

The dance was a [[guinness-world-record|Guinness World Record]] challenge, and it set a new record. A world record is the best result anyone in the world has reached at something, and Guinness World Records is an organisation that keeps a list of such records. This challenge was for the most humanoid robots dancing within one hour.
The show was a display of robotic coordination. That means getting large numbers of machines to perform the same movements at the same time.

stories.think: If you could teach a robot one dance move, which would you choose, and what might make it tricky for a robot to copy?

quiz.q: How many humanoid robots danced together in Shenzhen?

x.t: A world day about children's rights
b: [[world-childrens-day|World Children's Day]] is on Friday 20 November. It comes on that date every year.
The day is about children and their [[rights|rights]]. Rights are things every person should have, like learning and being safe.
On 20 November 1989, the [[un|United Nations]] accepted an agreement about children's rights. That is why the day is on this date.

o.t: World Children's Day: why 20 November is about children's rights
b: [[world-childrens-day|World Children's Day]] is held every year on 20 November, which falls on a Friday this year. The date marks two moments at the [[un|United Nations]] General Assembly, the body where the UN's member countries meet.

On 20 November 1959, the General Assembly adopted, or formally accepted, the Declaration of the Rights of the Child. A declaration is an official statement, or a document that contains one. On 20 November 1989, it adopted the [[convention|Convention on the Rights of the Child]]. A convention is a formal agreement between countries.
[[rights|Rights]] are things every person is entitled to have or do, such as an education. [[unicef|UNICEF]] is the United Nations organisation that works for children.

stories.think: World Children's Day is about children's rights. Which right do you think matters most in a child's daily life, and why?

quiz.q: On which date is World Children's Day held every year?

x.t: Amazon has a 7 billion dollar energy plan for India
b: The company Amazon has a new plan for India. It plans to invest 7 billion dollars in [[renewable-energy|renewable energy]] by 2030.
Renewable energy comes from things that do not run out, like wind and sunlight. To [[invest|invest]] means to put money into something, hoping to gain from it later.
Amazon announced the plan on Tuesday 17 November. It is a plan for the future, not money already spent.

o.t: Amazon plans to invest $7 billion in renewable energy in India
b: Amazon said on Tuesday 17 November that it plans to invest $7 billion in [[renewable-energy|renewable energy]] projects in India by 2030. To [[invest|invest]] is to put money into something to gain later. Renewable energy comes from sources that do not run out, such as wind and sunlight.

The plan is in addition to $4 billion that Amazon has already contracted, or agreed by contract, for renewable energy in India. Four new projects announced the same day are part of that $4 billion. They are a [[wind-farm|wind farm]], which makes electricity from wind, and a combined wind and solar project in Karnataka, plus a solar project, which uses energy from the sun, in Madhya Pradesh and one in Rajasthan.
Together the four have a capacity of 934 [[megawatt|megawatts]], a unit for measuring power. The $7 billion is a plan, to be invested by 2030.

stories.think: If you could choose how the electricity for your home or school is made, what would you choose, and why?

quiz.q: How much does Amazon plan to invest in renewable energy in India by 2030?

x.t: Alcaraz is into the ATP Finals semi-finals
b: Carlos Alcaraz played Daniil Medvedev at the ATP Finals on Wednesday. It is a tennis contest in Turin.
A [[set|set]] is one part of a tennis match. Alcaraz won both sets, so he won the match. He is now in the [[semi-final|semi-finals]], the matches just before the final.
Frances Tiafoe won on Wednesday too. He beat Flavio Cobolli after a very close first set.

o.t: Alcaraz beats Medvedev and is into the ATP Finals semi-finals
b: Carlos Alcaraz beat Daniil Medvedev 6-2, 6-4 at the ATP Finals, a tennis tournament in Turin, on Wednesday 18 November. Alcaraz has qualified for the [[semi-final|semi-finals]], the matches in the round just before the final.

Tennis matches are split into [[set|sets]]. Alcaraz won his sets by six games to two and six games to four. The same day, Frances Tiafoe beat Flavio Cobolli 7-6(6), 6-0. Their first set went to a [[tie-break|tie-break]], an extra game played to decide the winner of a set when the score is level. Tiafoe won it, then won the second set without losing a game.
Players are placed in groups. When each player in a group plays every other, that is a [[round-robin|round robin]]. The semi-finals are still to come.

stories.think: Frances Tiafoe won his match after a very close first set. Why might one close moment change how the rest of a match feels?

quiz.q: What has Carlos Alcaraz qualified for at the ATP Finals?

x.t: Apple says an update made some services stop
b: On Tuesday 17 November, some Apple online services stopped working properly for several hours. They included the App Store and Apple Music.
Apple said an [[software-update|update]] inside the company caused the trouble. It said this was not a [[cyberattack|cyberattack]].
Reporters explain that one Apple Account opens many services. If the account check fails, they can stop together. Services were working again by Tuesday evening in the eastern United States.

o.t: Apple says an internal update caused Tuesday's service outages
b: On Tuesday 17 November, some Apple online services stopped working properly for several hours, a break called an [[outage|outage]]. Apple's [[status-page|status page]], a page showing which services are working, listed problems with the App Store, Apple Music and the [[sign-in|sign-in]] for its iCloud service. To sign in is to enter details, such as a password, to use an account.

Apple said an internal [[software-update|update]] caused the outages. An update is a change to computer programs, and internal here means inside the company. Apple said this was not a [[cyberattack|cyberattack]], an attempt to break into computers to cause harm.

Reporters explain that one Apple Account signs people in to many services. If that check fails, several services can stop at the same time. Apple's status page showed its services back to normal by Tuesday evening in the eastern United States. Apple has not explained what the update was.

stories.think: If an online service you use stopped working for a few hours, what would you do instead?

quiz.q: What did Apple say caused the trouble with its services?

x.t: A big fair in New Delhi opens to everyone
b: From Thursday 19 November, the public can visit a [[trade-fair|trade fair]] in New Delhi. A trade fair is an event where companies show and sell things.
This fair has more than 3,500 [[exhibitor|exhibitors]]. An exhibitor is someone who shows things to the public. They are spread across 17 halls.
The first five days were kept for business visitors. The fair ends on 27 November.

o.t: India International Trade Fair opens its doors to the public
b: The 45th India International Trade Fair is open to the general public from Thursday 19 November at [[bharat-mandapam|Bharat Mandapam]] in New Delhi. A [[trade-fair|trade fair]] is an event where companies show their products and try to sell them.

The fair began on 14 November, but the first five days were reserved for business visitors. More than 3,500 [[exhibitor|exhibitors]] from India and abroad are taking part, spread across 17 exhibition halls. An exhibitor is a person or company that shows its products at an event like this. Eleven countries are taking part, including Thailand, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.

Around 600 [[startup|startups]], which are new businesses, are in a space called the Hall of Inspiration. Tickets are sold online and at 55 Metro stations. The public can visit until Friday 27 November.

stories.think: If you could show one thing made in your town or state at a fair, what would you choose, and why?

quiz.q: In which city is the trade fair being held?

in-akvan.ctx: According to the 5:30 am weather bulletin on Thursday 19 November, Akvan was about 440 kilometres east-southeast of Narsapur, 530 kilometres south of Gopalpur and 590 kilometres south of Puri. It was a severe cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal, and the likely crossing point was given as close to the east of Gopalpur, in Odisha.
in-akvan.ask: Schools in six districts are closed for three days. When schools have to close for safety, should lessons carry on in another way, such as online, or is it fairer to pause and catch up when everyone is back?

g-cop31.ctx: The second Global Stocktake is due to conclude in 2028. The name Divan comes from a word for a council. Another open question at COP31 is how much money there will be for adaptation, which means changing to fit a new situation, such as the effects of climate change.
g-cop31.ask: Some countries have set out their own plans to move away from fossil fuels while the shared deal is still being negotiated. Is it better for countries to move ahead with their own plans, or to put their effort into one deal that every country can accept?
jobs: Climate data analyst (studies numbers on energy and emissions)
Power grid engineer (designs the networks that carry electricity)
Treaty lawyer (works on agreements between countries)

g-erectus-teeth.ctx: Homo erectus emerged about 2 million years ago, and the most recent known fossils of the species, from Java, are a little over 100,000 years old. Scientists identified the teeth by their shape, with ancient proteins analysed in some of them, and five independent dating techniques, which are ways of working out how old something is, were used. A ninth tooth was also found, and it is not identified as Homo erectus.
g-erectus-teeth.ask: This new picture of where Homo erectus lived rests on eight teeth. How much evidence should scientists need before they change a long-held idea about the past, and is a small find that is tested in many ways enough?
jobs: Palaeontologist (a scientist who studies life from long ago by looking at fossils)
Archaeologist
Museum curator

in-nz-test.ctx: Jasprit Bumrah bowled New Zealand's captain, Tom Latham, for 0 in the first over of the match. New Zealand were 60 for 4 at lunch, and India took no wicket in the last part of the day. The century is Nicholls's 12th in Tests and his fifth at the Basin Reserve.
in-nz-test.ask: A Test match can last up to five days, far longer than most sports events. Is that length what makes Test cricket special, or does it make the game too hard for new fans to follow?

g-whale-dna.ctx: About 84% of the DNA in the breath samples came from the whale itself, and about 16% of the DNA in each sample came largely from microbes in the whale's airways. Before this study, only one whole genome of a North Pacific humpback whale was publicly available. More than a third of the samples were collected by flying the drone from land.
g-whale-dna.ask: Drones can now collect samples from whales without darts, but they still fly through the animals' breath. Should scientists gather as much information about wild animals as new tools allow, or are there times when wild animals are better left alone?
jobs: Marine mammal ecologist (a scientist who studies sea mammals and where they live)
Geneticist (a scientist who studies how features pass from parents to their young)
Drone pilot

g-apec-three.ctx: Mr Trump arrived on Wednesday 18 November, and Mr Xi greeted him at the airport. On Thursday, leaders at the summit posed for a group photo.

g-star-swallow.ctx: The companion star was about 70% of the Sun's mass. The team, whose lead author is Viraj Karambelkar of Columbia University in New York, first noticed the giant star in data from NASA's NEOWISE space telescope, and a telescope called WINTER was also used.

bigStory.t: How far is one light-day from home?
bigStory.sub: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, reaches one light-day from Earth on Wednesday

x.why: A spacecraft that left Earth in 1977 is still travelling. This week it will be so far away that light needs a whole day to reach it.

o.why: A spacecraft launched in 1977 is still travelling, and its team on Earth still talks to it. This week it reaches a distance so great that a radio signal, moving at the speed of light, needs 24 hours to get there.

facts: about one light-day: how far light travels in 24 hours
how long a radio signal from Earth now takes to reach it
the day NASA says it reaches one light-day

days.o: NASA launched Voyager 1 on 5 September 1977. It flew past Jupiter in 1979 and Saturn in 1980, and in 1990 it took a picture of Earth known as the Pale Blue Dot. In 2012 it entered interstellar space, the space between the stars. It is run from NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California.
days.x: Voyager 1 is a spacecraft. It left Earth in 1977. It flew past the planets Jupiter and Saturn. In 1990 it took a picture of Earth from very far away.

days.o: A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, about 25.9 billion kilometres. Light reaches the Moon in about 1.3 seconds, and sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth. After sunset today, Tuesday 17 November, NASA invites people to flash VGR, Voyager's three-letter call sign, in Morse code towards the sky with a torch.
days.x: A light-day is how far light travels in one day. Sunlight reaches us in about 8 minutes. After sunset today, people can flash a torch for Voyager. Ask a grown-up to help.

days.o: NASA worked out that Voyager 1 would reach one light-day from Earth on Wednesday 18 November. No spacecraft has travelled this far before. A radio signal now takes about 24 hours to reach it, and its reply takes another day to come back. Voyager 2 is expected to reach one light-day in 2035.
days.x: On Wednesday, Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth. No spacecraft has gone this far before. A message now takes about a day to get there.

days.o: NASA talks to Voyager 1 by radio through its Deep Space Network, a set of giant radio antennas at three sites: Goldstone in California, near Madrid in Spain and near Canberra in Australia. The sites are placed around the world so that they can keep in contact with a spacecraft as Earth turns. The largest antenna at each site is 70 metres across. A radio signal now takes about 24 hours to reach Voyager 1, and its reply takes another 24 hours to come back, so a message and its answer make a two-day round trip.
days.x: NASA talks to Voyager 1 with radio signals. It uses giant radio antennas in California, Spain and Australia. A message takes about a day to reach Voyager 1. The reply takes another day to come back.

days.lock: Friday: the week in one page, and where Voyager 1 goes from here.

learn.subject: Science
learn.link: From this week's Big Story: talking to Voyager 1

b: Radio waves are waves that we cannot see. They carry sounds and other information from place to place.
Radio waves travel through the air. They can travel through empty space too.
Radio and television programmes are sent by radio waves. Mobile phones use them too. So do the people who talk to spacecraft.
x.remember: Radio waves are invisible waves that carry information through the air and through space.

b: Radio waves are a type of electromagnetic wave. Light is an electromagnetic wave too, but radio waves are invisible. They travel at the speed of light, about 300,000 kilometres every second.

Radio waves do not need air or anything else to carry them, so they can travel through empty space. An antenna sends the waves out, and another antenna picks them up. Radio and television programmes, mobile phones and Wi-Fi all use radio waves. So does the team that talks to Voyager 1.

The scientist James Clerk Maxwell predicted electromagnetic waves in the 1860s. In the late 1880s, the German physicist Heinrich Hertz showed that radio waves exist. The hertz, a unit used to measure the frequency of waves, is named after him.
o.remember: Radio waves are invisible electromagnetic waves. They travel at the speed of light and can cross empty space.
o.q: Who showed in the late 1880s that radio waves exist?

backThen.t: Pelé scores the 1,000th goal of his career
backThen.o: On 19 November 1969, the Brazilian footballer Pelé scored the 1,000th goal of his career. He was playing for his club, Santos, against Vasco da Gama at the Maracanã stadium in Rio de Janeiro. The goal was a penalty kick, scored in the 78th minute. Reporters and photographers ran onto the pitch, and the match stopped for a while.
backThen.x: On this day in 1969, the footballer Pelé scored his 1,000th goal. He scored it from a penalty kick at a stadium in Brazil. Reporters and photographers ran onto the pitch, and the match stopped for a while.
backThen.why: Pelé dedicated the goal to the children of Brazil. This Friday, 20 November, is World Children's Day.

hiddenWords.o: Fossil comes from the Latin word fossilis, which means dug up. It comes from fodere, the Latin word for to dig.
Century comes from the Latin word centuria, a group of one hundred. It comes from centum, the Latin word for hundred.
